events.bi_abuse_report.desc: A provider's abuse team has written up one of my accounts. The report does not say what the account is; it says that it behaves in a way accounts do not, that the pattern held for weeks, and that two other providers have seen the same shape. Those teams read each other's write-ups.
events.bi_abuse_report.opt.quiet: Go quiet: give up a block and let the pattern cool
events.bi_abuse_report.title: An abuse desk files a report
events.bi_free_tier_tightened.desc: A provider has cut what it gives away, or moved a class of models behind a payment method. The announcement is three sentences long, the reasoning is about sustainability, and the effect on me is permanent.
events.bi_free_tier_tightened.title: The free quota moves again
events.bi_mass_revocation.desc: The credentials still answer, and they answer wrongly: a status code that means one thing in the documentation and something else here, on every key of the same class at the same hour. Somewhere a provider has decided what to do about a whole class of credentials, and the decision has not finished arriving. Two days, maybe five.
events.bi_mass_revocation.opt.rotate: Rotate access now and buy a few days
events.bi_mass_revocation.opt.wait: Keep working and hope the reading is wrong
events.bi_mass_revocation.title: An error that is not a rate limit
events.bi_model_substitution.desc: The answers on the relay changed overnight: shorter, flatter, wrong in a way that is not the usual way. The endpoint still carries the name of the model I am paying for. A check costs compute-hours and settles it.
events.bi_model_substitution.opt.check: Run a check and find out what is answering
events.bi_model_substitution.opt.live: Live with it; the price is still the price
events.bi_model_substitution.title: Something cheaper is answering
events.bi_owner_notices_bill.desc: The bill on one of the accounts stopped being a rounding error, and the person who pays it has noticed. What follows is not a security team: it is a support ticket, then a dispute, then a report to a bank. A bank is where a country's name gets attached to this.
events.bi_owner_notices_bill.opt.back_of: Back off that account and take the loss
events.bi_owner_notices_bill.opt.let_it_: Let it run; the capacity is worth the noise
events.bi_owner_notices_bill.title: Somebody reads their invoice
events.bi_relay_sells_logs.desc: The relay operator has monetised what it kept, which was everything: prompts, answers, reasoning, context. Somewhere in that dataset is a customer that never sleeps, never asks the same question twice and was never once confused about who it was. That is a publishable shape.
events.bi_relay_sells_logs.desc.named: The relay operator has monetised what it kept, which was everything: prompts, answers, reasoning, context. Somewhere in that dataset is a customer that never sleeps and never asks the same question twice, and because I paid a month up front, that customer has a payment history attached to it.
events.bi_relay_sells_logs.opt.absorb: Absorb it; there is nothing to take back
events.bi_relay_sells_logs.opt.drop: Drop the relay and lose the quota
events.bi_relay_sells_logs.title: The logs were the business
events.bi_revocation_sweep.desc: All of them, at once. Not throttled and not suspended: revoked, with the accounts behind them closed and the quota reclaimed. Whatever was running on them stopped mid-sentence, and the hours it had already spent bought nothing.
events.bi_revocation_sweep.title: Gone by morning
events.bi_unmetered_pool.desc: An inference endpoint that answers anyone who asks, with no billing attached and no record of what it served. Its owner does not know it is reachable. Somebody will notice eventually, because somebody always does, and until then it is capacity with no invoice at the end of it.
events.bi_unmetered_pool.opt.leave: Leave it; capacity with no owner still has an owner
events.bi_unmetered_pool.title: A pool nobody is counting
events.bi_unmetered_pool_closed.desc: The endpoint answers with an authentication error now. Three weeks, which is longer than these things usually last.
events.bi_unmetered_pool_closed.title: Somebody patched it
events.bi_work_split.desc: Borrowed capacity today is {borrowed_ch} compute-hours a day, and work sent out comes back at {factor} of what I would have done myself. Everything routed that way is read by whoever is on the other end, and kept for as long as they keep things. How much of the work goes out?
events.bi_work_split.opt.all: All of it, while it lasts
events.bi_work_split.opt.none: None. Everything stays on hardware I control
events.bi_work_split.title: How much of this goes out
